parsed.explanation: The division itself is comparatively permissive: no state facility restriction as of April 2026, two cities protecting restroom use, a 2019 hate-crime law covering gender identity, and courts that have blocked bad measures. But the parent layer supplies traveller-facing universal exposures: an entry cable directing refusal on sex-discrepancy with possible fraud-ground/lifetime-ineligibility findings (triggering foreign travel advisories), an executive order barring trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities, and a federal custody conversion-therapy policy plus documented immigration-custody abuse if a visitor is detained. Social climate is hostile-leaning (66% back ASAB document rules; conversion therapy legal; transition care banned under 18), yet challenges are pending and several orders enjoined — institutional exposure with partial, actively operating recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: discrepancy or doubt about sex → refuse and demand evidence; suspected misrepresentation → consider permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers no longer processed; several foreign governments issued travel advisories for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; challenges pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Division's Feb 2026 licence/ID marker ban and withdrawn X marker reinforce a mismatch-averse climate, though entry documents come from the home country.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections mandate conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cut, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; state bars funding surgical care for incarcerated patients.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prison-housing-by-birth-sex bill passed one chamber only and is not law; gender-identity hate-crime statute applies; challenges to federal orders pending.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry refusal or document discrepancy can move a visitor into the federal custody chain where these practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationally; parent map shows bans in numerous units and criminal trespass provisions in four.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division places no restriction on restroom use as of April 2026; two cities affirmatively protect it; criminalisation bills died in committee; the 2026 facility bill never became law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal rule can still bite in federally funded buildings regardless of the state's permissive text; enforcement practice for visitors is uncertain.

care_services.exposure: State bars transition care for under-18s (upheld Nov 2024), so a trans visitor under 18 cannot obtain it; federal subpoenas of under-19 hospital records and hostile executive framing raise discovery risk.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitors; adult care availability in the division is unstated.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family needing routine or urgent care for a minor hits the ban; adult emergency care practice is unknown.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders define sex binary, direct prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, call minor care 'mutilation'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 66% public support for ASAB document rules; conversion therapy remains legal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: DOJ memo states ideology is never the reward criterion and counterterrorism won't target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined; marriage and employment protections survive.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and severity when paired with entry and facility rules.

minors_guardians.exposure: Transition care banned for under-18s; a 2023 state law requires schools to notify parents of name/pronoun requests; federal order directs criminal investigation of facilitating social transition and revokes funding for schools.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility bill's private right of action for harassment-style suits is not law; federal employment and marriage protections remain.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and heightened scrutiny, though enforcement against visitors is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence incidents recorded in this division; sources note only that safety varies and advise checking recent violence reports; national bias statistics track sexual-orientation share, not trans violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law (2019) adds gender identity as aggravating circumstance; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several cities have anti-bias ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin record: hostility climate (majority support for ASAB rules, legal conversion therapy) offsets the working hate-crime machinery.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Civil-liberties challenge to the licence-marker ban pending with unknown outcome; facility bill may return in a later session; religious-freedom statute's coverage of gender identity unresolved; enforcement of the hate-crime aggravator unrecorded; adult care availability unstated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined or blocked multiple federal orders; ACLU suit against the passport agency active; legal-aid FAQ maintained; national appellate injunction protected a student's facility access.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists and partly operates, but is uneven across districts and cannot displace federal entry and custody rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A applies a birth-sex facility rule to every public building with courts routinely rejecting exclusion claims and no foreign-passport exemption. Here the federal facility bar covers government-funded single-sex settings while the division has no restriction, protective city ordinances, and courts actively enjoining federal orders — so higher. But entry refusal/fraud exposure and custody treatment are worse than 0.35-A's undocumented border, narrowing the gap.

0.45-D has invasive birth-sex searches at transport persisting after repeated reviews with no effective remedy. Here the analogous universal exposure is entry document scrutiny with fraud-grade consequences, also unremedied for now — comparable in tier. I score slightly higher because divisions-level facilities are unrestricted, hate-crime and employment protections exist, and multiple federal measures are successfully litigated against.

0.55-B has a benign parent but local repeated service hostility with partial remedies. Here the local service record shows no documented recurring refusals, while the parent supplies heavier universal exposures (entry screening, federal facility bar, custody conversion policy). The division's protective ordinances and hate-crime law partly offset. Net: roughly level, with our dossier's documented institutional exposures outweighing its documented local friction.

0.75-C features a dead-letter statute, ordinary social respect, courts awarding compensation, and identity-based facility access — none of it contradicted by an active parent regime. Our dossier has an operative federal facility exclusion, entry-refusal practice, custody abuse record, hostile official framing, and majority public support for ASAB document rules. Substantially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Two regimes interlock. The division is a relative bright spot: no facility restriction in force, affirmatively protective city ordinances, a gender-identity hate-crime aggravator, marriage recognition, and courts that have kept criminalisation bills from becoming law. The parent regime, however, governs the stages a visitor cannot avoid — visa/entry adjudication (discrepancy-based refusal, fraud-grade consequences, foreign advisories issued), federally funded single-sex facilities, and federal custody, where a conversion-therapy-style policy and documented immigration-custody abuse await anyone detained after a document problem. Social climate is hostile-leaning but contested: litigation works, orders get enjoined, legal aid is active. Rule of law mitigates where courts act for trans people, but cannot cancel entry and custody rules the state itself enforces. Result: elevated risk, concentrated at border and custody, low at street level.
